 About the Team   
 The HIL Platform and Services team in GM’s Autonomous Vehicle (AV) Organization   is responsible for   d eveloping and scaling high-fidelity , reliable Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) validation platforms that test AV software before   it’s   deployed to vehicles. Our platforms ensure enterprise usability, end-user functionality, and high-quality, use-case-driven signals for AV performance validation and AV system reliability.   

 We build and   operate   the systems that let AV teams   validate   perception , planning, control, and AI models against real hardware interfaces and complex scenarios, long before they reach the   road.   

About the Role   
 As a Software Engineer on the HIL Platform and Services team, you will be at the intersection of AV software and AI models and the hardware systems that enable vehicle autonomy. You will help shape what it takes to run, deploy, and test software on the next generation of GM   AVs.   Yo u   will work closely with teams across the AV   organization   – including Embodied AI, Model Deployment, Middleware, OS, Sensor Applications, and Vehicle Integration – to build the software and tooling that make large-scale HIL validation possible.   

 This is an   early-career   / new graduate role designed for candidates   who have recently or will be completing their degree by June 2026.   You will be paired with experienced engineers to help you ramp up on   AV Software, the   Software   HIL   platform and   services   concepts ,   and our internal   HIL   platforms   t hemselves . 

What   You’ll   Be Doing (Responsibilities)   

 Develop software to increase the capabilities, fidelity, observability, and scale of our HIL platform and integration services.   

Build and extend services and tools that make it easy for AV teams to configure, run, and debug tests on HIL benches.   

Deliver reliable software through clear   requirements   generation, continuous integration, automated testing, issue tracking, and code reviews.   

Collaborate with colleagues across multiple AV teams to understand their validation needs and translate them into platform features.   

Deliver complex projects through incremental development, iterating quickly while   maintaining   quality and reliability.   

Basic Qualifications (Required)   

 Currently has, or is   in the process of obtaining   a Bachelor or   Master's degree in Computer Science   or relevant technical field.     

Degree must be completed prior to joining GM   

Strong systems fundamentals (for example, data structures, algorithms, operating systems, or computer architecture) and solid coding abilities in Python and/or C++,   demonstrated   through coursework, internships, or   substantial   projects.   

Understanding of   how to design high-performance software components (for example, from systems, OS, networks, or performance-sensitive projects).   

Experience developing in a Linux environment (class projects, labs, research, or internships all qualify).   

Ability to work effectively in a collaborative, cross-functional team, with clear written and verbal communication.   

Preferred Qualifications (Nice to Have)   

 Experience   optimizing   or evaluating complex software systems on dedicated hardware (for example, GPUs, embedded boards, FPGAs, or custom test rigs).   

Exposure to ROS   architectures ( r obotics   projects, labs, or internships).   

Experience with low-latency or real-time systems (for example, control loops, real-time simulations, or latency-sensitive services).   

Prior   exposure to the autonomous driving, robotics, or real-time simulation domains (internships, research, or   substantial   personal projects).   

Experience with SQL   

Familiarity with a large build system such as Bazel,   CMake , or similar for multi-language, multi-target projects.

jobs.title: Software Controls Engineer - Power Electronics
jobs.location: Milford, Michigan, United States of America
jobs.description:
Job Description 
 Work Classification: 
 
 Hybrid: The successful candidate is expected to report to Milford, MI three times per week, at minimum, or as dictated by the business.

The Role: 
 
 General Motors is seeking a motivated Software Engineer to join the Battery Energy Transfer organization. This role develops embedded software for electrified vehicles, with a focus on power-electronics control and energy-transfer functions such as onboard charging, power conversion, charging and discharging, and vehicle-to-everything capabilities.
 
 You will design, implement, integrate, and validate production-quality software that enables safe, reliable, and efficient transfer of energy between the vehicle, battery, and charging infrastructure. The role combines hands-on embedded software development with system-level collaboration across software, controls, systems, validation, calibration, electrical architecture, and hardware teams.
 
 What you’ll do: 
 
 Develop and maintain embedded C/C++ software for automotive power-electronics and energy-transfer applications.

 Design software for AC/DC charging, DC/DC conversion, voltage and current regulation, power-flow control, state machines, diagnostics, protection, and fault handling.

 Translate system and controls requirements into clear, maintainable, and testable software designs and implementation.

 Collaborate with software architects, system engineers, SSLEs, hardware and HWIO teams, calibration, validation, and suppliers to resolve technical issues and deliver integrated solutions.

 Support software architecture, interface definition, feature decomposition, and requirements traceability from system behavior through implementation and test.

 Develop and review software using sound design principles, coding standards, and automotive embedded best practices, including MISRA-aligned development where applicable.

 Use CAN and other vehicle communication technologies to support controller interfaces, diagnostics, and feature integration.

 Perform unit, integration, hardware-in-the-loop, system, and vehicle-level testing; investigate failures and drive root-cause resolution.

 Support automated build, test, and continuous-integration workflows to improve software quality and delivery efficiency.

 Use behavior- and test-driven development practices, including clear acceptance criteria and Given/When/Then scenarios where appropriate.

 Participate in design reviews, code reviews, technical problem solving, and continuous improvement of development and validation processes.

 Contribute to charging and energy-transfer features supporting EV charging infrastructure, charging protocols, and bidirectional energy-transfer use cases.

Your Skills & Abilities (Required Qualifications): 
 
 Bachelor’s degree in Software Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Controls Engineering, or a related field.

 2+ years of professional experience in automotive embedded software development, power-electronics controls software, or a closely related field.

 Demonstrated hands-on experience developing production-oriented software in C or C++.

 Understanding of real-time embedded software design, software interfaces, state machines, diagnostics, and hardware/software integration.

 Experience translating requirements into software design, implementation, and verification activities.

 Experience with software debugging, integration, root-cause analysis, and automated or bench-based testing.

 Ability to work effectively across software, systems, controls, hardware, validation, and other cross-functional engineering teams.

 Strong written and verbal communication skills, analytical ability, and attention to detail.

What Will Give You a Competitive Edge (Preferred Qualifications): 
 
 Master’s degree in a relevant engineering or computer science discipline.

 5+ years of professional experience in automotive embedded software development, power-electronics controls software, or a closely related field.

 Experience with onboard chargers, OBCM systems, AC/DC converters, DC/DC converters, power-factor correction, voltage/current control, or related power-electronics applications.

 Experience with automotive charging, discharging, EVSE interfaces, V2X, V2G, or charging protocols such as DIN/ISO, CCS, NACS, or CHAdeMO.

 Knowledge of CAN, LIN, Ethernet, ARXML, UDS, or other automotive communication and diagnostic technologies.

 Familiarity with requirements and traceability tools such as DNG or DOORS, and development tools such as Git, Jira, CANoe/CANalyzer, or equivalent platforms.

 Experience with software architecture, MBSE concepts, automated testing, CI/CD pipelines, or DevOps practices.

 Experience with HIL, SIL, CoSim, bench, dyno, or vehicle-level validation.

 Knowledge of functional safety, cybersecurity, ASPICE, MISRA, or other automotive software quality practices.

 Experience with BDD or TDD methods and writing behavior-focused, testable requirements.

What will help you succeed: 
 
 Strong interest in electrification, power conversion, and automotive embedded software.

 Ability to move between detailed code-level problem solving and system-level technical discussions.

 Ownership mindset, curiosity, and willingness to resolve issues through collaboration.

 Commitment to building safe, maintainable, testable, and reusable software.

 Ability to work in an agile environment and manage priorities across multiple stakeholders.

Relocation benefits are available for candidates who qualify under company policy.

 As a member of the Vehicle Safety, Engineering & Defense Research Lab, you will be working with the Biometrics & Sensing research group.  You will be applying your expertise in autonomous vehicles, driving simulators, human factors, and data science for developing innovative approaches to immersive user studies for automated driving-enabled vehicles.  As a researcher in this group, you will implement your solutions in driving simulators and publish your research findings in peer-reviewed journals to extend the reach of General Motors’ development of next-generation technology. This will also include interfacing with universities, research institutes, and other advanced technology laboratories to build a network for amplifying your research.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer – Autonomy Evaluation
jobs.location: Sunnyvale, California, United States of America
jobs.description:
Job Description 
 General Motors is a global leader in advanced driver   assistance . With   Super Cruise   hands-free technology in more than 500,000 Super Cruise–equipped vehicles on the road and over 700 million hands-free miles driven, GM is proving that automation can be trusted, intuitive, and helpful. GM has the global reach to bring   cutting-edge   advances to everyday drivers at   unprecedented   scale. Join us to help deliver the next generation of safe and delightful personal autonomous vehicle experiences.   

 About the Organization     

The   Evaluation team   builds and evolves the evaluation ecosystem that powers the development and scaling of GM’s autonomous driving technology. We develop metrics, automated workflows, and analysis approaches that enable data-driven decisions across AV development and verification. Partnering with Autonomy, Simulation, Systems, and Safety teams, we act as system-level integrators and arbiters of end-to-end AV quality.   

We own large-scale test scenario libraries, continuous evaluation pipelines, and critical risk assessment and release-gating components, treating road testing, data mining, training, and metrics as first-class use cases in a unified analytics framework. By joining this team, you will help shape GM’s core evaluation platforms, turn system-level results into clear feedback for engineering and leadership, and help accelerate validated AV deployment at scale.   

What   You’ll   Do (Responsibilities)   

 Architect and implement metrics and analyses to introspect autonomous driving software performance at   subsystem   interfaces across the autonomy stack; partner closely with autonomy developers and systems engineers.   

Design and implement analysis algorithms that summarize, aggregate, and cluster metrics produced by simulations and on-road runs of the autonomy stack.   

Propose and develop new statistical and ML methods to quantify performance and   identify   patterns of system and subsystem behavior across diverse scenes and operational domains.   

Develop and apply methods to introspect the operation of ML components in the autonomy stack, including evaluation of   perception , prediction, and planning models.   

Build and   maintain   autonomy   evaluation   dashboards and interactive reports that provide clear, explainable insights (e.g., trend analysis, drift detection, scenario coverage) for development, verification, and leadership.   

Leverage vision-language models (VLMs) and large language models (LLMs), where   appropriate , to classify autonomy performance,   identify   critical scenarios, and prioritize validation efforts, integrating human-in-the-loop review where needed.   

Maintain a high technical standard through thoughtful system design, code reviews, testing, observability, and adherence to software-engineering best practices.   

Interface with cross-organizational partners to articulate requirements, resolve handoff issues, and share best practices around evaluation, metrics, and experiment design.   

Your Skills & Abilities   (Required Qualifications)   

 5+ years of applied experience with robotics or autonomous systems software (e.g., sensors,   perception , prediction, planning, or control), data analysis, ML evaluation, or autonomy analytics.   

3+ years evaluating dynamic systems using numerical and/or ML approaches, including time-series data, state derivatives, dynamics, and interconnected subsystems.   

Strong   proficiency   developing   Python   in production team environments, including testing, performance, and code review.   

Proficiency   with   Pandas, NumPy, SciPy ,   and plotting/visualization libraries for large-scale data analysis and reporting.   

Comfort working with   C++   codebases, including reading, debugging, and instrumenting core algorithms.   

A strong curiosity to question anomalous data and systematically root-cause discrepancies.   

Demonstrated technical leadership, including driving architectural decisions, influencing cross-team designs, and owning complex features or services end-to-end.   

Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD in   C omputer Science, Robotics, Mechanical or Aerospace Engineering, Machine Learning, Data Science , or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.    

What Will Give You a Competitive Edge (Preferred Qualifications)   

 Experience in   a utonomous driving or field robotics , including visualizing and interpreting results from simulation and field experiments.   

Experience evaluating robotics or AV systems using   sensor data   (e.g., camera, lidar, radar) and large-scale   time-series   analysis.   

Strong intuition for   data visualization   and the ability to decompose high-dimensional metrics into clear, trustworthy, and consumable views for technical and non-technical audiences.   

Familiarity with   statistical modeling, experimental design, and hypothesis   testing   for autonomy or simulation evaluation; fluency with Pandas, NumPy, SciPy, and visualization tools.   

Proficiency   in   C++ and SQL ; experience shaping logging, data schemas, and evaluation pipelines for large-scale autonomy testing and performance monitoring.   

Experience working with   ROS or similar robotics/IPC frameworks , log pipelines, and large-scale experiment databases or evaluation platforms.   

Prior development experience with   computational geometry, linear algebra,   PyTorch , and ML techniques applied to   perception , prediction, planning, or control.   

Background in modeling   agent interaction   and contributing to   release gating   and safety decisions for autonomy systems.   

Experience   leveraging   AI-assisted development and analytics tools   to improve productivity and evaluation coverage.

jobs.title: Autonomous Vehicle Test Engineer
jobs.location: Yuma, Arizona, United States of America
jobs.description:
Job Description 
 Position summary
 GM Level: 6A

 Proposed job-family alignment: Test and Validation Engineering

 Primary work location: GM Desert Proving Ground, Yuma, Arizona

 Travel: Approximately 10% as needed for training, team alignment, vehicle support, or other GM testing activities

 Career track: Individual contributor

General Motors is developing advanced driving-assistance and autonomous-vehicle capabilities that require safe, repeatable, and scalable validation. The AV Test Engineer will be the onsite technical lead for a focused closed-course testing operation at GM’s Desert Proving Ground in Yuma, Arizona.
 
 This role will own day-to-day technical execution for a small assigned fleet of approximately two to three autonomous test vehicles. The engineer will plan and execute closed-course regression, feature, behavior, calibration, and other structured testing; coordinate limited operations personnel supporting the work; and ensure the vehicles, test setup, track activities, data, and results are ready to support engineering and program decisions.
 
 Yuma is intentionally a lean operating environment. There will not be dedicated technicians or additional engineers permanently onsite to provide routine support. The successful candidate must be a self-starter who can operate independently, recognize and resolve common vehicle and AV-system issues, and know when to stop testing or escalate to remote engineering, Service Operations, Fleet Reliability Engineering, Vehicle Integration, or other partners. The role requires comfort moving between test planning, driving and observing closed-course scenarios, vehicle health checks, troubleshooting, data handling, and clear technical communication.
 
 The position is especially important during the winter testing season, when Yuma provides a weather-resilient location to maintain closed-course testing capacity when conditions or schedule constraints limit testing elsewhere. The engineer will help make the local fleet and facility a dependable, repeatable testing capability rather than a temporary campaign location.
 
 What you’ll do
 Lead onsite closed-course testing
 Serve as the onsite technical lead for all assigned AV closed-course testing activities at Yuma, translating approved test requests and engineering objectives into executable plans, procedures, schedules, and resource requirements.

 Plan and execute repeatable software regression, feature and behavior validation, structured scenario, calibration, fault-response, and targeted data-collection tests.

 Coordinate daily test sequencing, track reservations, vehicle assignments, operating windows, safety reviews, and test readiness with remote AV Test Engineering and cross-functional stakeholders.

 Direct and brief limited operations personnel supporting test execution, including task assignments, vehicle preparation, track setup, lead-vehicle or target support, run sequencing, communications, and post-run closeout.

 Provide clear technical direction during test execution while maintaining the distinction between engineering ownership and operations execution responsibilities.

 Make timely onsite decisions about whether a test is ready to proceed, should be modified, should be repeated, or must be stopped and escalated based on vehicle condition, system behavior, track conditions, weather, data quality, or safety risk.

 Support extended or non-standard testing schedules when required by release timing, track availability, seasonal priorities, or campaign needs, consistent with site and safety requirements.

 Own the assigned Yuma test fleet
 Act as the primary technical owner for approximately two to three assigned AV test vehicles, maintaining awareness of their configuration, software and calibration state, physical condition, instrumentation, data-recording readiness, and current availability.

 Perform or coordinate daily vehicle checkouts, pre-drive readiness checks, post-drive inspections, charging or fueling coordination, sensor and camera cleanliness checks, hard-drive or data-media handling, and other activities required to keep vehicles test-ready.

 Manage vehicle configuration and test preparation activities, including approved software or branch deployments, calibration updates, route or map selection, logging configuration, test tools, and required test assets.

 Maintain accurate vehicle status, mileage or test-hour records, configuration information, test history, open issues, and return-to-service decisions for the local fleet.

 Identify vehicle downtime risks early and develop practical containment, recovery, and escalation plans to protect testing availability.

 Coordinate parts, materials, shipping, facility resources, charging support, and remote technical assistance when onsite needs exceed available capability.

 Build and maintain a winter-readiness plan for the Yuma fleet, including vehicle availability, spare equipment, data-storage capacity, charging or fueling needs, test assets, operating procedures, and contingency plans.

 Troubleshoot vehicle and AV-system issues
 Perform first-line technical triage for issues involving the AV software stack, vehicle compute, sensors, localization, calibration, connectivity, data recording, host-vehicle systems, vehicle networks, power or charging, and test infrastructure.

 Use vehicle symptoms, operator observations, system status, logs, drive data, diagnostic tools, and repeatable experiments to isolate likely causes and determine the next action.

 Reproduce issues when safe and practical, capture accurate timelines and evidence, and create actionable issue reports for remote engineering or support teams.

 Distinguish between issues that can be safely contained or corrected onsite and issues requiring vehicle removal from service, engineering review, formal change control, or additional safety assessment.

 Partner with Troubleforce, Service Operations, Fleet Reliability Engineering, Vehicle Integration, AV software and hardware teams, and other remote experts to drive issues toward resolution.

 Support controlled fault-injection or non-nominal testing when requested, ensuring that test intent, expected system response, safety controls, and data-labeling requirements are understood before execution.

 Develop practical troubleshooting guides, recovery procedures, checklists, and escalation paths that reduce dependence on ad hoc support and improve repeatability for future Yuma personnel.

 Deliver high-quality test results and data
 Execute test procedures consistently and capture complete run information, including vehicle, software, calibration, map, track, scenario, operator, weather, and timing details.

 Evaluate AV behavior and system response against defined test objectives and acceptance criteria, distinguishing objective evidence from anecdotal observations.

 Capture and communicate pass, fail, blocked, incomplete, and inconclusive outcomes with enough context for engineering teams to act without repeating avoidable setup work.

 Ensure drive links, logs, hard drives or data media, notes, screenshots, issue references, and other required evidence are transferred or uploaded through approved workflows.

 Review test data for completeness, corruption, missing signals, unexpected configuration changes, or other conditions that could limit its usefulness.

 Publish concise test summaries and status updates to the appropriate engineering and operations forums, and maintain traceability in tools such as Jira, Confluence, Xray, Slack, and approved data or fleet-management systems.

 Provide timely feedback to remote software, systems, simulation, safety, and program teams so that test results support release decisions, feature refinement, and issue prioritization.

 Establish a dependable Yuma operating model
 Help stand up and continuously improve the permanent Yuma closed-course testing capability, including roles, standard work, readiness gates, communications, operating rhythms, and handoffs with the broader AV Test Engineering and AV Operations organizations.

 Maintain a repeatable intake-to-execution workflow for local test requests, including request clarification, prioritization, planning, execution, results reporting, and issue follow-up.

 Create and maintain onsite documentation for vehicle checkout, test preparation, track use, safety controls, data handling, troubleshooting, emergency response, and end-of-day closeout.

 Coordinate with DPG Site Operations, Safety, Infrastructure, Mapping, security, and other facility partners to ensure the local operation meets site requirements and has the resources needed to execute safely.

 Track local performance indicators such as vehicle availability, test hours, completed runs, blocked runs, downtime, repeat failures, data-upload timeliness, issue aging, and test-request cycle time.

 Identify opportunities to increase usable testing hours, reduce avoidable setup and reset time, improve vehicle utilization, and shift repeatable work to appropriately trained operations personnel.

 Capture lessons learned from winter testing and other campaigns and convert them into improved test plans, asset requirements, procedures, and recommendations for future scaling.

 Maintain a Safety First culture
 Follow all GM, DPG, AV Operations, AV Test Engineering, and applicable safety procedures and work controls.

 Verify that required personnel, training, vehicle qualifications, test equipment, track conditions, emergency support, communications, and approved procedures are in place before testing begins.

 Stop work and escalate when vehicle condition, system behavior, weather, track conditions, personnel readiness, facility conditions, or test setup creates unacceptable risk.

 Maintain the requirement that testing is conducted with appropriate onsite personnel and never rely on unsupported lone-person operations or unapproved after-hours activity.

 Support incident, near-miss, and abnormal-event documentation with accurate facts, timelines, evidence, and follow-up actions.

 Required qualifications
 Bachelor’s degree in mechanical, electrical, automotive, systems, computer, robotics, aerospace engineering, computer science, or a related technical discipline.

jobs.title: Battery State Estimation Senior SW Engineer
jobs.location: Milford, Michigan, United States of America
jobs.description:
Job Description 
 DUTIES: Design, develop, and productionize robust battery state estimation algorithms for SOC, SOH, and SOP using physicsbased, modelbased, and hybrid datadriven estimation techniques across multiple battery chemistries. Develop observers and filters (e.g., equivalent circuit and electrochemical informed models, Kalman filter based approaches) that remain accurate across temperature extremes, power transients, sensor noise, and battery aging. Incorporate calendar and cycle aging effects into estimation logic so outputs remain truthful throughout the battery lifecycle and across chemistries and pack architectures. Implement estimation algorithms as production quality embedded software in C/C++, meeting GM standards for safety, cybersecurity, and coding discipline, including MISRA compliance. 10% domestic travel required. Hybrid Work Policy - 3 days In-office, 2 days remote - Must be able to report to local office. 

REQUIREMENTS : Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related field of study and Five (5) years of experience as a Software Engineer, Design Engineer, Automotive Engineer, or related occupation. Two (2) years of experience with: Delivering embedded software for high voltage battery systems; SOC, SOH, and SOP estimation algorithms deployed in vehicles; C/C++ for embeddedsystems development; Agile/Scrum environments and cross functional automotive programs; and Leveraging Battery Data to generate actionable insights that improve batteryperformance, reliability, and lifecycle characteristics.

 About The Role: 
 
General Motors is transforming how we develop and validate embedded controls and software as we move toward our Zero Crashes, Zero Emissions, Zero Congestion vision. We are seeking a Staff Software Architect – Mechatronics Controls Simulation to lead the technical architecture of simulation environments supporting GM’s Vehicle Body Controls domain (vehicle access, cabin thermal, occupant positioning, occupant protection, lighting, visibility, vehicle state, and related functions) within the Virtualization & SIL Integration (VnSI) organization.
 
 In this role, you will own the end-to-end simulation architecture for the Vehicle Body Controls domain, define and govern CoSim packages, and lead variant and configuration management across programs and model years. You will partner closely with Simulation Integration Engineers (SIEs), System Integration Architects, Software Architects, and SW Quality Architects to ensure our simulation solutions are scalable, robust, and fully integrated into continuous integration (CI) pipelines for GM’s Software Defined Vehicle (SDV) Architecture.
 
 Key Responsibilities: 
 Provide technical and architectural leadership for the Vehicle Body
Controls domain simulation, setting the long-term vision and roadmap for
simulation capabilities and infrastructure.
 Define and maintain the simulation architecture for the Vehicle Body
Controls domain, addressing functional and non-functional requirements
(performance, fidelity, scalability, reusability, maintainability) and align
with SDV and Mechatronics Infrastructure direction.
 Define the variant and configuration management strategy for simulation
packages across programs, regions, model years, and option content (e.g.,
trim levels, content packages, regulatory variants).
  Collaborate with System Engineers and SIEs to define Simulation Bills of
Materials (SIMBOMs) that map program test requirements and feature
content into concrete CoSim assets for each configuration.
 Establish and maintain standards for simulation package structure,
documentation, versioning, and release notes to ensure traceability and
ease of deployment across virtual test environments and CI pipelines.
 Own the simulation architecture for behavioral modeling for systems
outside of the test boundary, defining how networks, ECUs, and vehicle
behaviors are represented in simulation.
 Define the architectural strategy and technical enablers required to scale
CI/CD across simulation packages, virtual ECUs, and test environments.
  Partner with pipeline and tools teams to align test packages with CI quality
gates (e.g., build, smoke tests, regression suites, coverage criteria) and
ensure failures are actionable by teams.

drive alignment across simulation, software, and systems engineering
organizations.
 Contribute to, and in some cases lead, training and lunch-and-learn

management, and CI practices.

 Bachelor’s degree in Electrical / Computer / Mechatronics Engineering,

engineering, or controls, with substantial time spent on simulation,
SIL/HIL, or co-simulation for automotive or similar safety-critical domains.

tools (e.g., Git, GitHub Actions, gcc/gdb, Eclipse or similar).

simulation technical lead with responsibility for architecture across
multiple programs or domains.
  Deep hands-on experience with test environments, including integration of
controls, plant models, and communication models for embedded
controllers.
 Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional technical discussions, drive
consensus, and make trade-offs across performance, quality, and delivery.
Preferred Qualifications
 Master’s or PhD degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or a related
field.
  Prior Staff-level (or equivalent) experience defining and leading the
architecture of complex embedded or simulation systems that span
multiple Electronic Control Units (ECUs), vehicle domains, and feature sets.
  Experience designing or operating continuous integration pipelines for
embedded software, including quality gates, promotion strategies, and
automated regression selection.
 Proficiency with MATLAB/Simulink for plant and/or behavior model
development and integration, and familiarity with FMU/FMI and SSP
standards.
 Solid knowledge of automotive communication technologies (CAN, LIN,
automotive Ethernet) and experience modeling or configuring network
behavior in simulation.
 Hands-on experience designing or leading variant and configuration
management strategies for embedded software, simulation, or test
environments.
 Familiarity with AUTOSAR layered software architecture and integration of
AUTOSAR-based ECUs into CoSim environments.
  Experience with cloud-hosted simulation / virtualization platforms and
scaling test execution on shared infrastructure.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, Autonomy Evaluation
jobs.location: Remote - United States
jobs.description:
Job Description 
 General Motors is a global leader in advanced driver   assistance . With   Super Cruise   hands-free technology in more than 500,000 Super Cruise–equipped vehicles on the road and over 700 million hands-free miles driven, GM is proving that automation can be trusted, intuitive, and helpful. GM has the global reach to bring   cutting-edge   advances to everyday drivers at   unprecedented   scale. Join us to help deliver the next generation of safe and delightful personal autonomous vehicle experiences.   

About the Organization    

 The   Evaluation team   builds and evolves the evaluation ecosystem that powers the development and scaling of GM’s autonomous driving technology. We develop metrics, automated workflows, and analysis approaches that enable data-driven decisions across AV development and verification. Partnering with Autonomy, Simulation, Systems, and Safety teams, we act as system-level integrators and arbiters of end-to-end AV quality.   

 We own large-scale test scenario libraries, continuous evaluation pipelines, and critical risk assessment and release-gating components, treating road testing, data mining, training, and metrics as first-class use cases in a unified analytics framework. By joining this team, you will help shape GM’s core evaluation platforms, turn system-level results into clear feedback for engineering and leadership, and help accelerate validated AV deployment at scale.   

What   You’ll   Do (Responsibilities)   

 Architect and implement metrics and analyses to introspect autonomous driving software performance at   interfaces across the autonomy stack; partner closely with autonomy developers and systems engineers.   

Design and implement analysis algorithms that summarize, aggregate, and cluster metrics produced by simulations and on-road runs of the autonomy stack.   

Propose and develop new statistical and ML methods to quantify performance and   identify   patterns of system and subsystem behavior across diverse scenes and operational domains.   

Develop and apply methods to introspect the operation of ML components in the autonomy stack, including evaluation of   perception , prediction, and planning models.   

Build and   maintain   autonomy   evaluation   dashboards and interactive reports that provide clear, explainable insights (e.g., trend analysis, drift detection, scenario coverage) for development, verification, and leadership.   

Leverage vision-language models (VLMs) and large language models (LLMs), where   appropriate , to classify autonomy performance,   identify   critical scenarios, and prioritize validation efforts, integrating human-in-the-loop review where needed.   

Maintain a high technical standard through thoughtful system design, code reviews, testing, observability, and adherence to software-engineering best practices.   

Interface with cross-organizational partners to articulate requirements, resolve handoff issues, and share best practices around evaluation, metrics, and experiment design.   

Your Skills & Abilities   (Required Qualifications)   

 5+ years of applied experience with robotics or autonomous systems software (e.g., sensors,   perception , prediction, planning, or control), data analysis, ML evaluation, or autonomy analytics.   

3+ years evaluating dynamic systems using numerical and/or ML approaches, including time-series data, state derivatives, dynamics, and interconnected subsystems.   

Strong   proficiency   developing   Python   in production team environments, including testing, performance, and code review.   

Proficiency   with   Pandas, NumPy, SciPy ,   and plotting/visualization libraries for large-scale data analysis and reporting.   

Comfort working with   C++   codebases, including reading, debugging, and instrumenting core algorithms.   

A strong curiosity to question anomalous data and systematically root-cause discrepancies.   

Demonstrated technical leadership, including driving architectural decisions, influencing cross-team designs, and owning complex features or services end-to-end.   

Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD in   C omputer Science, Robotics, Mechanical or Aerospace Engineering, Machine Learning, Data Science , or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.   

What Will Give You a Competitive Edge (Preferred Qualifications)   

 Experience in   a utonomous driving or field robotics , including visualizing and interpreting results from simulation and field experiments.   

Experience evaluating robotics or AV systems using   sensor data   (e.g., camera, lidar, radar) and large-scale   time-series   analysis.   

Strong intuition for   data visualization   and the ability to decompose high-dimensional metrics into clear, trustworthy, and consumable views for technical and non-technical audiences.   

Familiarity with   statistical modeling, experimental design, and hypothesis   testing   for autonomy or simulation evaluation; fluency with Pandas, NumPy, SciPy, and visualization tools.   

Proficiency   in   C++ and SQL ; experience shaping logging, data schemas, and evaluation pipelines for large-scale autonomy testing and performance monitoring.   

Experience working with   ROS or similar robotics/IPC frameworks , log pipelines, and large-scale experiment databases or evaluation platforms.   

Prior development experience with   computational geometry, linear algebra,   PyTorch , and ML techniques applied to   perception , prediction, planning, or control.   

Background in modeling   agent interaction   and contributing to   release gating   and safety decisions for autonomy systems.   

Experience   leveraging   AI-assisted development and analytics tools   to improve productivity and evaluation coverage.

Job Description 
 This role is categorized as hybrid. This means the successful candidate is expected to report to Warren, Michigan three times per week, at minimum 

 The Role 
 This position offers the opportunity to work in a highly collaborative team focused on propulsion related system models including thermal, hydraulic, lubrication and ventilation domains. Build 1D fluid dynamics & coarse 3D thermal models that directly impact design development, validation and eliminate hardware testing. Simulations include battery cell, battery pack, drive units, electric motors, power electronics, combustion engine and transmission related systems. 

 What You'll Do 
 Conceptualize, build, and exercise analytical system level models for electrified and conventional propulsion systems using 1D software tools (GT-SUITE, AMESIM, MATLAB, Simulink or similar)

 Own and advance analysis practices and/or tools to improve prediction fidelity and execution speed
 Collaborate with analysis counterparts across several VDDV teams representing global propulsion systems and vehicle engineering
 Mentor, train and lead our TCS India colleagues as well as new team members
 Provide technical leadership and problem resolution by leveraging analysis results
 Lead efficiency improvement projects, including the development of automation tools via Python or MATLAB

 Bachelor of Science in Engineering
 5+ years of experience with simulation, design, testing, or release of propulsion related systems
 1 year of experience with GT-SUITE, AMESIM or similar software
 Extensive experience with the principles of vehicle propulsion system design, operation, or testing
 ​

 Master of Science in Mechanical or Aerospace Engineering with coursework in heat transfer or fluid mechanics

 Experience in AI / ML methods or Agentic workflows.

Job Description 
 At General Motors, our product teams are redefining mobility. Through a human-centered design process, we create vehicles and experiences that are designed not just to be seen, but to be felt. We’re turning today’s impossible into tomorrow’s standard —from breakthrough hardware and battery systems to intuitive design, intelligent software, and next-generation safety and entertainment features.   
 
 Every day, our products move millions of people as we aim to make driving safer, smarter, and more connected, shaping the future of transportation on a global scale. 
 
 Hybrid: This role is categorized as hybrid. This means the successful candidate is expected to report to Warren, MI three times per week, at minimum.
 
 The Role 
 The Thermal Systems Simulation Integration Engineer plays a critical role in advancing the transition to virtual engineering by leading the integration of full-vehicle, cross-functional co-simulation models with a focus on Thermal Systems and related domains. This role is responsible for enabling high-fidelity, system-level simulation capabilities that support faster, data-driven engineering decisions.
 
 This is a highly collaborative position, requiring partnership across Vehicle Design, Development & Validation (VDDV), Vehicle Performance, Validation, SMT, and VMEC teams to ensure seamless integration and alignment of simulation tools and methodologies.
 
 As part of an emerging and rapidly evolving space, success in this role requires a passion for innovation, continuous improvement, and the ability to navigate and influence across complex technical landscapes.
 
 What You’ll Do 
 Lead delivery of integrated co-simulation packages to enable virtual thermal systems design, development, and validation

 Lead resolution of program issues by rallying co-simulation partners to meet the demands of the problem

 Advocate for adoption of virtual methods for vehicle design, development, and validation

 Act as a single point of contact for Co-simulation users for thermal systems to resolve concerns on usage

 Forecast and plan needs and get support for required resources

 Define strategic opportunities for innovating processes and methods

 Align with software releases and calibration milestones to ensure the virtual vehicle co-simulation package is up to date

 Ensure Cosim packages meet standards as defined by the SIE governance team

 Represent the needs of thermal systems among SIE peers from other disciplines

 BS Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Software Engineering, Computer Science, or related field .

 Familiarity with system tools or controls integration CAE tools such as GT Power, AMESIM, Carsim, Carmarker, MATLAB/Simulink or other similar CAE tools.

 Proven ability to work in teams, balancing technical theory with practical limitations.

 Strong oral and written communication skills.

 MS Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Software Engineering, Computer Science, or related field.

Job Description 
 The Role 
 As a Software Engineer on the Galileo team, you will design, build, and scale the infrastructure and technology that powers testing and evaluation workflows for vehicle release and autonomous driving stack validation and verification. This includes developing and optimizing data processing pipelines, backend services, and internal tools used for large-scale analysis. In this role, you will independently own significant technical areas, drive high-quality implementation from design through production, and partner with cross-functional teams to build systems that support AV / ADAS development. You will help raise the engineering bar through sound technical judgment, strong execution, and mentorship of other engineers.
 
 About the Organization 
 The GM AV Simulation team builds world-class testing and analysis products and technologies to help accelerate development of autonomous vehicles and broader vehicle software systems. Our customers range from AV developers understanding the effects of their code on vehicle behavior, to data engineers using our pipelines for evaluation insights, to release teams tracking top-line performance metrics. AV Simulation aims to deliver intuitive user experiences for robotics and AI engineers that help move GM toward a driverless future. Galileo is building the core infrastructure and architecture to support testing at scale. As part of this team, you will help build and evolve the infrastructure required for test organization, test triggering, test analysis workflows, and related data pipelines.
 
 What You’ll Do
 Design, develop, and maintain software systems that support large-scale autonomous driving evaluation workflows

 Own major components and services that enable simulation, test execution, analysis, and reporting at scale

 Build and improve infrastructure used to process and analyze large volumes of driving and evaluation data

 Drive reliable software delivery through strong engineering practices including code reviews, automated testing, observability, and continuous integration

 Collaborate across teams to define technical requirements, resolve ambiguous problems, and deliver scalable solutions

 Demonstrated experience building and operating high-quality production software systems

jobs.location: Markham, Ontario, Canada
jobs.description:
Job Description 
 Job Description 
 Vacancy Status:  
 This posting is not for an existing vacancy within the organization and is open to new applications. (New Head Count) 

 AI Disclosure: 
 As part of the application process, Artificial Intelligence will be used in the hiring process for this role. 

 Work Arrangement  
 Hybrid: This role is categorized as hybrid. This means the successful candidate is expected to report to Markham Elevation Centre (MEC) three times per week at minimum, or other frequency dictated by the business. 

 The Role: 
 
We are seeking a motivated software engineer to help verify and validate Propulsion Thermal Management functions across virtual, simulated, hardware-in-the-loop, and vehicle environments. In this role, you will translate system requirements and behavioral specifications into clear, traceable test cases, develop and execute automated system behavior tests, analyze results, and support the resolution of issues that affect vehicle software quality. 
 
The role is in the Vehicle Software and Electronics Engineering (VSEE) organization. The team is at the forefront of innovation, where vehicle software design, integration, release, and validation come together to improve engineering and quality processes. Your work will help ensure that thermal-management functions—including battery and propulsion-system temperature control, cabin conditioning, diagnostics, and degraded operating modes—perform as intended and support the delivery of high-quality GM vehicles. This work contributes to GM’s vision of a world with ZERO Crashes, ZERO Emissions, and ZERO Congestion. 

What You’ll do: 
 
 Translate Propulsion Thermal Management system requirements, system functions, and Behavioral Test Specifications (BTS) into clear, traceable system test cases, procedures, and acceptance criteria. Maintain linkage between requirements, test assets, execution results, and defects. 
 Develop, maintain, and execute automated System Behavior Tests (SBTs) and functional system tests for propulsion thermal functions across CoSim/SIL environments, with targeted validation on HIL benches and vehicles when real-time behavior, hardware I/O, or physical system response is required. 
 Validate end-to-end thermal-management behavior, including RESS/battery heating and cooling, power-electronics and drive-unit thermal protection, cabin heating and cooling, thermal request coordination and arbitration, sensor and actuator behavior, diagnostics, and degraded or remedial operating modes. 
 Support CoSim package readiness for Propulsion Thermal Management by checking package health, interfaces, configurations, virtual ECU behavior, plant-model connectivity, HWIO behavior, and environment sanity before broader regression or milestone testing. 
 Review automated regression results. Rapidly distinguish product/software defects from CoSim, plant-model, infrastructure, configuration, or test-script issues; perform initial root-cause isolation and route each issue to the appropriate owner. 
 Document failures with sufficient technical detail to reproduce the issue, including software and model versions, vehicle/environment conditions, calibrations or overrides, logs, expected versus actual behavior, and requirement/test-case references. Track defects through resolution and verify corrective actions through retest and regression. 
 Partner with Product System Engineers, System Owners, Functional System Architects, System/Sub-System Engineers, Software Quality Assurance Engineers, Software Integration Managers, calibration teams, and validation teams to define test scope, review BTS/STS content, resolve requirement ambiguity, and support TFRP milestone readiness. 
 Maintain test scripts, procedures, test data, dashboards, and supporting documentation for current software and CoSim releases. Share lessons learned, training materials, reusable test patterns, and best practices that improve consistency and reduce duplicated effort. 
 Participate in product, architecture, model, and test-environment reviews; provide actionable feedback on testability, observability, requirement quality, system boundaries, and end-to-end verification strategy. 
 
 Required Qualifications: 
 Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field. 
 Expected to graduate between December 2026 and June 2027. 
 Available to work full-time, 40 hours per week. 
 
 Preferred Qualifications: 
 Knowledge of vehicle thermal-management systems, including refrigeration cycles, refrigerant systems, HVAC, heat pumps, and associated controls
 Experience with automated testing frameworks, such as Robot Framework or Autobot, for system-level validation and regression testing. 
 Proficiency in programming or scripting using C, C++, Python, or comparable languages. 
 Familiarity with Behavior-Driven Development (BDD) processes and Gherkin syntax. 
 Experience using ETAS INCA, Intrepid Vehicle Spy, or similar data-acquisition and vehicle-network tools. 
 Experience with MATLAB and Simulink for plant-model development and integration; basic familiarity with simulation tools such as GT-Power, Amesim, or CarSim. 
 Familiarity with automotive communication technologies, including CAN, LIN, SPI, and automotive Ethernet. 
 Experience with virtualization, software integration, or virtual ECU environments. 
 Familiarity with visualization tools such as Power BI or Databricks dashboards to communicate technical insights effectively. 
 Familiarity with SQL and Databricks in an Azure Cloud environment. 
 Familiarity with data-storage solutions, databases, and data-processing frameworks. 
 Ability to translate business or engineering questions into data-driven solutions. 
 Experience developing or applying AI/ML-based solutions. 

Compensation:  
 The salary range for this role is $73,900 to $110,900. The actual base salary a successful candidate will be offered within this range will vary based on factors relevant to the position.

jobs.description:
Job Description 
 Why join us? 
At General Motors, our product teams are redefining mobility. Through a human-centered design process, we create vehicles and experiences that are designed not just to be seen, but to be felt. We’re turning today’s impossible into tomorrow’s standard — from breakthrough hardware and battery systems to intuitive design, intelligent software, and next-generation safety and entertainment features. Every day, our products move millions of people as we aim to make driving safer, smarter, and more connected, shaping the future of transportation on a global scale

 The Role 
 The Safety Assurance for Effective Autonomous Driving Software (SAFE-ADS) department is part of GM’s Global Product Safety, System, and Certification (GPSSC) organization. SAFE-ADS serves as a central body for automated driving system (ADS) safety assurance, bringing together technical expertise from across the company to support the safe development, testing, launch, and continuous improvement of advanced driving capabilities. 

 GM is seeking an Autonomous Vehicle Safety Case Technical Program Manager to lead the integrated execution of complex, cross-functional safety cases for ADS. This senior/staff individual contributor will bring structure, momentum, and transparency to the workstreams that support GM’s ADS safety case and safety assurance strategy. 
 The role will coordinate technical and operational work across safety case management, safety and risk management systems, operational safety and human factors, aggregate safety and rules-of-the-road metrics, counterfactual simulation, and related system-safety interfaces. The successful candidate will connect strategy to execution: translating safety objectives into actionable plans, aligning claims and sufficiency criteria with evidence and assessments, managing dependencies and risks, and driving decisions to closure across engineering, validation, operations, legal, public policy, and product teams. 

 This role is ideal for an experienced program leader who is comfortable operating in a technically complex, safety-critical environment; can synthesize diverse inputs into a coherent execution plan; and is motivated by the challenge of enabling the safe, measurable, and scalable deployment of ADS technology. 

 What You’ll Do  
 Integrated Program Leadership 
 Build and maintain integrated program plans covering safety case workstreams, milestones, dependencies, resource needs, risks, decisions, and deliverables. 
 Establish operating rhythms, governance forums, status reporting, action tracking, decision logs, and escalation paths that enable effective cross-functional execution. 
 Align safety case claims with ADS product, engineering, validation, operational, and launch milestones. 
 Translate evolving safety strategies and program objectives into clear workstream charters, measurable outcomes, delivery plans, and ownership models. 
 Identify schedule, scope, technical, evidence, resource, and cross-functional dependency risks; drive mitigation plans and escalate issues when needed. 
 Create clear, concise communications for technical teams, senior leaders, and cross-functional decision forums. 
 Safety Case and Assurance Execution 
 Coordinate the development, assessment, maintenance, and continuous improvement of ADS safety cases across product-launch contexts. 
 Drive alignment among safety claims, sufficiency criteria, evidence plans, assessment activities, and program milestones. 
 Establish and maintain traceability between safety strategies, claims, requirements, evidence, assessments, decisions, and changes in system scope or operating conditions. 
 Coordinate technical inputs from AI/ML, autonomy, systems engineering, functional safety, SOTIF, cybersecurity, software validation, simulation, human factors, operations, and product safety teams. 
 Track evidence readiness, assessment status, substantiation gaps, deviations, and corrective actions; ensure gaps are closed, actively managed, or supported by documented rationale. 
 Support impact assessments when the ADS, operational design domain, platform, release, feature behavior, or deployment plan changes. 
 Improve the processes, tools, and information flows used to manage the safety case and safety assurance lifecycle. 
 Continuous Improvement 
 Establish scalable methods for planning, prioritization, reporting, evidence management, and change control across SAFE-ADS. 
 Use program data and operational feedback to identify systemic issues, improve process health, and increase predictability of safety assurance delivery. 
 Promote early and frequent collaboration between safety assurance teams and the engineering and operations organizations developing and deploying ADS capabilities. 
 Help mature GM’s safety assurance practices as ADS technology, operating scope, evidence methods, and industry expectations evolve. 
 
 Your Skills & Abilities (Required Qualifications) 
 Bachelor’s degree in engineering, computer science, systems engineering, robotics, safety engineering, mathematics, or a related technical field. 
 7+ years of experience leading complex technical programs in autonomous vehicles, ADAS, software-intensive systems, systems engineering, product safety, safety assurance, or another safety-critical domain. 
 Demonstrated experience leading cross-functional programs with multiple workstreams, stakeholders, dependencies, and enterprise-level visibility. 
 Strong program management capabilities, including integrated planning, milestone management, dependency tracking, risk management, governance, issue resolution, and executive communication. 
 Experience translating ambiguous technical or safety objectives into structured execution plans, measurable outcomes, and clear ownership. 
 Experience developing, supporting, assessing, or managing safety cases, assurance cases, safety arguments, or equivalent evidence-based safety programs. 
 Working knowledge of safety assurance concepts and practices, including requirements traceability, evidence management, hazard or risk management, change control, and assessment processes. 
 Ability to understand and connect technical work across software, AI/ML, systems engineering, validation, simulation, human factors, operations, and product safety. 
 Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to tailor information for technical, operational, and executive audiences. 
 Ability to influence without authority, build alignment across functions, work through ambiguity, and drive action to closure. 
 Passion for autonomous vehicle technology and safe deployment of advanced driving capabilities. 
 
 What Will Give You a Competitive Edge (Preferred Qualifications) 
 Advanced degree in engineering, computer science, robotics, systems engineering, safety management, mathematics, or a related field. 
 Experience with autonomous vehicle or ADAS safety assurance, safety case management, safety management systems, or product launch readiness. 
 Experience with Goal Structuring Notation (GSN) or another structured argumentation framework. 
 Familiarity with functional safety, SOTIF, AI/ML safety, operational safety, human factors, rules-of-the-road compliance, or safety performance metrics. 
 Experience working in a fast-paced engineering organization with frequent software releases, evolving system scope, and complex technical dependencies. 
 Experience working with independent assessors, standards bodies, regulators, industry consortia, or external technical partners. 
 Program or project management certification.

 The salary range for this role is $160,200 to $290,700. The actual base salary a successful candidate will be offered within this range will vary based on factors relevant to the position.

 Benefits:  GM offers a variety of health and wellbeing benefit programs. Benefit options include medical, dental, vision, Health Savings Account, Flexible Spending Accounts, retirement savings plan, sickness and accident benefits, life insurance, paid vacation & holidays, tuition assistance programs, employee assistance program, GM vehicle discounts and more.

Note: program participants are required to purchase/lease a qualifying GM vehicle every four years unless one of a limited number of exceptions applies.

Job Description 
 General Motors is a global leader in advanced driver assistance. With Super Cruise hands-free technology in more than 500,000 Super Cruise-equipped vehicles on the road, and over 700 million hands‑free miles driven, GM is proving that automation can be trusted, intuitive, and helpful. GM has the global reach to bring cutting‑edge advances to everyday drivers at unprecedented scale. Join us to help deliver the next generation of safe and delightful personal autonomous vehicle experiences. 

The Evaluation team builds and evolves the evaluation ecosystem that powers developing and scaling GM’s autonomous driving technology. We develop metrics, automated workflows, and analysis approaches that enable data-driven decisions across AV development and verification. Partnering with Autonomy, Simulation, Systems, and Safety teams, we act as system-level integrators and arbiters of end-to-end AV quality. We own large scale test scenario libraries, continuous evaluation pipelines, and critical risk assessment and release gating components, treating road testing, data mining, training, and metrics as first-class use cases in a unified analytics framework. By joining this team, you will help shape GM’s core evaluation platforms, turn system-level results into clear feedback, and help accelerate validated AV deployment at scale.

 Define the strategy and architecture for metrics and analyses to evaluate autonomous driving software performance across the autonomy stack.

 PhD, Masters, or Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Robotics, Mechanical or Aerospace Engineering, Machine Learning, or a related field.

Experience in autonomous driving or high-stakes field robotics; designing, running, and interpreting large-scale simulation and field experiments.

 The Role
 You will be part of a team that drives systematic and data-driven improvements to autonomous vehicle software by designing, implementing, and maintaining robust processes for evaluation and validation. We are looking for a highly motivated individual with excellent analytical skills to own end-to-end execution, improve evaluation methodologies, and communicate insights that establish confidence in the quality of our end-to-end ML stack.
 
 In this position, you will work closely with AI/ML engineers, simulation engineers, systems engineers, and data partners to identify, analyze, monitor, and prioritize the signals used to assess performance. You will leverage simulation and on-road data to build scalable processes for evaluating coverage, metrics, uncertainty, and validation confidence.
 
 If you are interested in having a major impact on accelerating validation confidence for ML-driven autonomy through creative problem solving, let’s chat!
 What you’ll be doing
 Define AV evaluation and validation processes from initial concept through implementation, including test-framework requirements, scenario and test-suite design, coverage, metrics, and the evidence needed to assess confidence in system performance.

 Design and implement scalable testing and simulation frameworks for test generation, execution, data collection, result aggregation, and reproducible analysis.

 Provide hands-on implementation of infrastructure and data solutions to assess confidence in AV performance using simulation and on-road data.

 Develop and apply methods to evaluate simulation validity, sim-to-real correlation, and the predictive value of simulation results.

 Proactively scope and identify metrics, sampling approaches, and analytical methods needed to improve evaluation workflows and close gaps in evidence.

 Contribute to automated triage and root-cause analysis strategies for AV deficiencies, regressions, and uncertainty in an end-to-end stack.

 Articulate insights, summaries, limitations, and recommendations to engineers, technical leaders, and other stakeholders based on continuous analysis of AV performance.

 Define and maintain scalable processes to identify, monitor, and improve evaluation KPIs and confidence measures.

 Help connect continuous-improvement activities to the evidence needed to support safety, systems, and downstream readiness decisions.

 What you must have
 Strong Python programming skills, with experience building clear, maintainable analysis, evaluation, or testing tools.

 Experience designing or implementing testing, simulation, or evaluation frameworks for complex software/hardware or cyber-physical systems.

 Experience with GitHub, Jira, or equivalent tools.

 Demonstrated end-to-end ownership, from defining a problem through delivering and communicating the desired outcome.

 A track record of analytical and systems-engineering work involving complex software/hardware systems or ambiguous AI functions.

 Experience performing root-cause analysis and applying analytical methods to system or behavioral performance data.

 Ability to creatively solve problems with limited supervision, learn quickly, and operate effectively in a fast-paced environment.

 Strong cross-functional communication skills, including the ability to communicate data-driven findings to leadership.

 Bachelor’s, master’s, or doctoral degree in engineering, physics, applied mathematics, statistics, data science, or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

 Bonus points!
 Experience with autonomous vehicles, ADAS, robotics, or production-grade robotic systems.

 Hands-on experience with simulation environments, scenario generation, large-scale test execution, or analysis of simulation results.

jobs.description:
Job Description 
 DUTIES: Design, develop, and implement advanced controls and automation systems for automotive body shop manufacturing operations, ensuring system reliability, efficiency, and compliance with established engineering standards. Develop and document system requirements, functional specifications, and control strategies for automated manufacturing systems, including robotics, machine vision, and conveyance technologies. Program, configure, and troubleshoot Allen Bradley PLCs (including Safety Logic) and Siemens TIA Portal HMIs, ensuring seamless integration with plant wide automation systems. Design, implement, and maintain industrial communication networks—including EtherNet/IP, TCP/IP, and DeviceNet—to support real time communication across PLCs, robots, vision systems, and peripheral devices. Integrate, program, and optimize FANUC industrial robots for material handling, spot welding, dispensing, and vision guided operations. Develop, configure, and troubleshoot machine vision systems (Matrox, SICK, Keyence, Photoneo, FANUC Vision) for inspection, error proofing, and bin picking applications. Maintain and enhance vision guided bin picking solutions utilizing 3D vision technologies to increase automation efficiency and reduce manual handling. Support, maintain, and optimize conveyance systems, including Power & Free conveyors, Geo Pallet systems, skid conveyors, and Automated Guided Carts (AGCs), ensuring continuous and reliable production flow. Configure and troubleshoot Allen Bradley Variable Frequency Drives (PowerFlex, ArmorStart) and related motion control systems. Develop and implement error proofing systems such as torque verification (Atlas Copco), barcode readers (SICK, Matrox), RFID based tracking, and automated bin pick validation. Create and interpret electrical schematics using EPLAN to support system design, integration, commissioning, and troubleshooting. Perform root cause analysis of automation and controls failures using empirical data, trend analysis, diagnostic tools, and structured problem solving methodologies to drive corrective and preventive actions. Analyze manufacturing and operational data using DLA and Power BI (TBIA) to identify inefficiencies, improve throughput, and reduce downtime. Lead continuous improvement initiatives focused on cycle time reduction, downtime elimination, and quality improvements (e.g., DRR reduction). Provide real time production support, including troubleshooting, maintenance assistance, and system optimization for high volume manufacturing lines. Develop and maintain custom engineering tools and applications to support automation systems, data analytics, and production performance monitoring. Ensure standardization, scalability, and reuse of automation components across new installations, upgrades, and major projects. Identify system vulnerabilities and implement 
 mitigation strategies to improve system reliability, robustness, and safety. Track, document, and report corrective actions, ensuring full closure and compliance with engineering and quality standards. Collaborate with cross functional partners—including manufacturing, quality, and maintenance—to support system integration, launch readiness, and production goals. Stay current with emerging technologies, industry trends, and best practices in industrial automation, robotics, and smart manufacturing. Hybrid Work Policy – 3 days In-Office, 2 Days Remote – Must be able to report to local office.

jobs.location: 2 Locations
jobs.description:
Job Description 
 The Role   

 General Motors is building the next generation of software-defined vehicles and advanced driver-assistance experiences. The success of these products depends on understanding how they perform in the real world, how customers experience them, and where product and engineering investment will create the greatest benefit.   

As a   S enior   Data Scientist ,   S uper Cruise (SC)   and   Assisted Driving and Active Safety ( ADAS )   Insights, you will be a hands-on technical and strategic partner to Product Management, Systems Engineering, Data Engineering, Safety, and Program teams. You will turn complex vehicle telemetry, retail-fleet data, engineering data, and customer-behavior signals into trusted metrics, actionable insights, and clear recommendations that shape product strategy and prioritization.   

You will help product teams understand feature availability, usage,   evaluate feature availability,   utilization , safety performance, reliability, customer acceptance, and trust-related behaviors across Super Cruise , advanced autonomy   products   and ADAS products .   

This is a senior individual-contributor role for someone who can independently frame ambiguous problems, develop rigorous analyses, influence decisions without formal authority, and   establish   analytical practices that scale across the organization.   

What   You’ll   Do   

 Partner with Product Management to translate product questions into analyses that inform strategy, roadmaps, requirements, prioritization, investments, and launch decisions.   

Define and   maintain   trusted KPI frameworks for   AV,   Super Cruise and ADAS, including metric definitions, assumptions, data lineage, limitations, baselines, thresholds, and   appropriate use   of engineering and retail-fleet data.   

Evaluate product performance across availability, usage, effectiveness, customer value, and experience,   identifying   drivers, tradeoffs, risks, opportunities, regressions, and regional or population-level differences.   

Build integrated datasets, models, dashboards, scorecards, recurring reports, and self-service tools that connect vehicle, driver, safety-event, trip, crash, and operating-context data to support ongoing monitoring and action.   

Investigate unexpected trends and data-quality issues, partnering with engineering and data teams to address gaps in signals, triggers, decoding, sampling, instrumentation, and data availability.   

Apply sound statistical and causal-inference methods to vehicle data, evaluations, feature rollouts, and constrained experiments, and communicate findings and recommendations effectively across technical teams, cross-functional forums, and senior leadership.   

How   You’ll   Make an Impact   

 Product teams use a common, trusted view of   performance rather than disconnected or conflicting analyses.   

Retail-fleet data becomes a practical input to product strategy, release decisions, regional expansion, and engineering prioritization.   

High-value customer and safety problems are quantified, ranked, and connected to specific product or engineering actions.   

Product teams can distinguish true performance changes from changes in data coverage, instrumentation, fleet mix, software releases, or analytical definitions.   

New metrics and data use cases are developed with   appropriate privacy ,   access-control , regulatory, and data-retention considerations.   

Decision-makers   receive clear narratives that explain what changed, why it matters, what is uncertain, and what should happen next.   

Your Skills & Abilities (Required Qualifications)   

 Bachelor’s degree in Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Engineering, Economics, or a related quantitative discipline, or equivalent practical experience. A master’s degree is preferred.   

5   or more years of experience in data science, product analytics, applied statistics, or a closely related field.   

Expert-level SQL skills and strong experience working with large, complex, evolving data environments.   

Strong Python skills for data preparation, exploratory analysis, statistical analysis, visualization, automation, and reproducible analytical workflows.   

Demonstrated experience defining metrics,   validating   datasets,   identifying   data-quality issues, and explaining analytical limitations.   

Experience using observational data to evaluate product performance, customer behavior, feature adoption, reliability, safety, or operational outcomes.   

Demonstrated ability to translate ambiguous product or business questions into rigorous analysis and actionable recommendations.   

Experience influencing product roadmaps, prioritization, investment decisions, launch decisions, or requirements through data and analysis.   

Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical concepts and uncertainty to non-technical stakeholders.   

Ability to   operate   with substantial autonomy, exercise sound judgment, and deliver results across multiple teams without direct reporting authority.   

What Will Give You a Competitive Edge (Preferred Qualifications) 

Experience working with automotive, connected-vehicle, ADAS, autonomous-driving, robotics, mobility, or other safety-critical products, including vehicle telemetry, sensor and fleet data, operational statistics, event recording, and driver-assistance systems such as Super Cruise .   

Experience with Databricks, Spark, Azure, GCP, Power BI, Tableau, Looker, or comparable data and visualization platforms.   

Experience with metric catalogs, data contracts, data governance, instrumentation strategy, data sampling, human labeling, or analytical quality standards.   

Experience with causal inference, quasi-experimental methods, rollout analysis, survival or reliability analysis, hierarchical modeling, or other methods appropriate for real-world product data.   

Experience working with privacy, legal, regulatory, or data-access constraints in the development of customer or vehicle-data use cases.   

What Success Looks Like in the First 12 Months   

 Establish a trusted analytical partnership with SC Product Management and Systems Engineering.   

Deliver a prioritized set of SC performance insights that directly   informs   roadmap or investment decisions.   

Improve the definition, validation, or usability of key SC topline and trust- eroding-behavior   metrics.   

Establish repeatable release-over-release and retail-fleet performance analyses for agreed priority metrics.   

Contribute analytical evidence to at least one launch, regional expansion, or major   software-release   decision.   

Identify   material gaps in data, instrumentation, sampling, or metric quality and drive practical resolutions with partner teams.   

Create reusable analytical assets that reduce ad hoc work and improve product-team self-service.   

Extend the approach to one or more Active Safety or Assisted Driving use cases.
